symptom: if … then <return> else end if; laid the unhappy branch on the main row (530;200, end 690;200) and moved the happy path to 840;200, so the false flow was drawn through the branch; without the else the branch sat on its own row (530;300).
cause: Six layout sites asked `s.HasElse || len(s.ElseBody) > 0`, and isGuard required !HasElse, so an empty `else` (recorded by the visitor for round-tripping) turned a guard into an IF/ELSE layout. HasElse is read nowhere but the layout.
fix: ifHasElse: an else branch is a non-empty ELSE, or an empty one after a THEN that carries on. isGuard and all six sites use it; builder and measurer stay in agreement because they share the predicate.
insight: A flag that only says what the source spelled is not a layout fact. When the builder and the measurer each test the same condition inline, change it in one named predicate, or the two drift and positions overlap. Compare the two spellings' layouts in one test — the model is identical, so the layout must be.
test: mdl/executor/layout_empty_else_guard_2204_test.go (empty else == no else, branch on its own row, no overlaps; control: empty else after a continuing THEN keeps its merge); reverted: the reported 530;200/690;200
